spec_match.rationale: Six detection candidates evaluated live and graded against the DOM/HTML-spec end state (HTMLUnknownElement, vanished interface object), plus a config-first slot pattern that genuinely calls runAdAuction before choosing a branch — the removal-migration shape invariant 7 asks for.

interactive.rationale: Evaluate-every-check, fill-the-slot, a force-removal toggle and clear all run live; the slot really renders an iframe with the fallback reason printed.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index promises six graded detection candidates and a slot that keeps filling by asking for a config, which is exactly what the page does.

edge_cases.rationale: The createElement-truthiness trap and version-sniffing-vs-field-trial cases are both graded misleading with reasons; the slot covers no-config, no-element and forced-removal branches, each with its own printed reason.

references.rationale: References live on the feature index (chromestatus, spec, intent thread); this concept page carries none itself — the per-page link nit is recorded on the sibling critique.

conformance.rationale: The suite's createelement-never-returns-null and htmlunknownelement assertions are literally the first and third rows of this page's matrix, and ran 4/4 on this browser.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) via CDP: the matrix evaluated with 4 of 6 checks graded surviving (truthiness and UA checks correctly marked misleading on this pre-removal build); Fill-the-slot took the fallback branch with the verbatim https-seller TypeError as the printed reason and rendered the iframe (slot.html loaded); the force toggle re-rendered via the forced branch; console clean, no exceptions; screenshots both viewports.

telemetry_health.rationale: Good namespaced logging, but like its siblings the page does not load /public/demo-telemetry.js, so the triage pipeline never sees it.

design_system.rationale: Token colours, secondary button and checkbox accent-color from tokens, focus-visible outlines, scroller-wrapped matrix.

accessibility.rationale: role=status outputs, aria-live slot, labelled 44px toggle, captioned scoped table, titled frames, good/bad verdicts as text plus colour.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: 0px horizontal overflow at 360x740 DPR3 and 1280x800 over CDP; the matrix scrolls internally on mobile and both screenshots are clean.

openQuestions.title: Re-drive the matrix on a real Chrome 155 build to convert predictions into observations
openQuestions.detail: On this pre-removal Chromium 141 the 'once the element is gone' column is still a prediction for every row (the feature-level critique carries the same caveat). When a 155 stable build is available to the harness, re-run the matrix and slot there and update the touched critiques with the observed post-removal values — especially instanceof HTMLUnknownElement flipping to true and the slot falling back for the no-element reason instead of the no-config reason.

summary: The migration page every removal should ship: the wrong check is demonstrated wrong, the right pattern is executed rather than pasted, and the slot filled through its fallback with the auction's verbatim refusal as the printed reason — verified over CDP on Chromium 141 headless (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp) at http://localhost:3000/v155/remove-fencedframe-element-and-window-fence-apis/shipping-through-the-removal/, including the force-removal branch; console clean, no overflow on either class; feature /conformance/ route 4 pass / 0 fail. Open item: observe the post-removal column on a real 155 build.
